topic: Open WebUI v0.13.3 ships agents in automations
thesis: Open WebUI v0.13.3 lets a scheduled automation run a coding agent in the terminal and folder you chose, so your first unattended agent errand is three moves away.
explanation_path: Begin with the thing the viewer already does: asking a model in a chat to fix something, and the wall they hit -- the fix lives in a chat window and dies there. Introduce the terminal as the hands: one connected computer workspace with a real folder turns the same chat into an agent that reads and writes files. Name the gate that has kept this attended: tool calls wait for a person to click Allow, so agent runs needed someone present. Reveal what the schedule adds: an automation is the same prompt with a clock on it, run by the server whether or not a browser is open. Land the release's actual move -- the automation editor now saves the terminal, the folder and the coding agent together with the schedule, and checks that they are still available before a run starts. Show where the evidence lands: a real chat holding the whole run, and a run-history line marked success or error. Finish on the guardrail the docs state themselves: unattended runs execute with full tool approval because nobody is there to click Allow, so the first folder should be a throwaway and the prompt should say what not to touch.

claims.claim: Open WebUI v0.13.3, dated 2026-11-08 in the changelog, adds Agents in automations: the automation editor now lets you choose a terminal and a working folder, then select a coding agent available there.
Scheduled runs reuse the saved terminal and folder and check that both the terminal and the agent are still available before starting, and agent automations send their results to a chat.
The coding agents in question are named tools -- Claude Code, Codex and Pi -- which have appeared in the model picker on agent-capable Open Terminals since v0.13.1, dated 2026-11-03.

Scheduled runs execute with full tool approval because nobody is there to click Allow, so Open WebUI's own guidance is to give the task a workspace you are comfortable with and a prompt that says exactly what to do, and what not to.

Every scheduled run produces a real chat in the selected workspace, visible in the sidebar with the full task activity, plus a run-history entry on the task showing success or error with the error text.

Tether, introduced in this release cycle, is the desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that ties your own computer to Open WebUI, connecting outward so there are no ports to open, with a renewable session that expires after 90 days without use by default.
The open-webui repository shows 158.2k stars, 683 watching and 23.0k forks on GitHub as accessed 2026-11-09.

claims.claim: Automations are created under User Menu > Automations with a New Automation button, and support Once, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly and Custom (RRULE) schedule modes, with Daily, Weekly and Monthly running at the exact minute you pick in your own timezone.

A terminal is connected under Settings > Admin > Integrations in the Open Terminal section, by clicking + and entering the terminal URL such as http://localhost:8000 plus the API key chosen during installation.

misconceptions.myth: The agent keeps working only while I keep the browser tab open.
misconceptions.reality: Automations run server-side on their schedule, and every run leaves a real chat and a run-history entry whether or not anyone was watching (claims 2 and 5).

misconceptions.myth: Unattended is safe because the agent will stop and ask before doing anything risky.
misconceptions.reality: Scheduled runs execute with full tool approval -- nobody is there to click Allow -- which is exactly why the docs say to pick a workspace you are comfortable with and write instructions that state what not to do (claim 4).

glossary.definition: A self-hosted web interface, run on your own machine or home server, that fronts local and cloud AI models.
A saved prompt that Open WebUI runs on a schedule; each run creates a real chat.
The connected computer workspace (a real shell and filesystem) that lets a model run commands and edit files instead of just chatting.
An AI coding tool such as Claude Code, Codex or Pi that edits code in a folder on its own.
The desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that links your own computer to Open WebUI.
The directory the agent works in for a run; the boundary you chose for it.
The Allow click a normal chat requires before the model runs a tool such as a shell command.
The iCalendar recurrence syntax behind custom schedules, e.g. RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0 for every day at 09:00.
The per-task list of past runs, each marked success or error with the error text.

suggested_outline:
Hook: while you slept, a coding agent ran inside a folder you picked -- Open WebUI v0.13.3 put agents inside automations.
Recall the familiar starting point: asking a model in a chat to fix something, and the fix dying in the chat window.
Add the hands: one connected terminal with a real folder turns chat into an agent that reads and writes files.
Name the old wall: tool calls wait for Allow, so agent runs needed a person in the chair.
Deliver the release's move: the automation editor saves the terminal, the folder and the agent with the schedule, and checks they still exist before each run.
Show the three viewer moves on screen: connect the terminal, create the automation and pick terminal, folder, agent, then hit Run now.
Show where the evidence lands: a real chat with the whole run, and a run-history line marked success or error.
Honest catch: unattended means full tool approval, nobody clicks Allow, so start with a throwaway folder and a prompt that says what not to touch.
notes: Conflict, not averaged: the automations docs page (source 3) states The automation editor has no terminal setting. A run uses the terminal configured on the model it runs, while the v0.13.3 release notes (source 1) state the editor now lets you choose a terminal and working folder directly. This brief follows the release notes: they are first-party, dated 2026-11-08, and describe the newer behavior; the docs page appears not yet updated for v0.13.3 (it also omits agent selection). Consequence for the script: present terminal, folder and agent selection as living in the automation editor per the release note, and do not teach the older configure-terminal-on-the-model path as the current flow. Same-day releases: the changelog dates both 0.13.2 and 0.13.3 as 2026-11-08; v0.13.2 contained only fixes, so what is new vs 0.13.2 is exactly the agents-in-automations editor, terminal and folder switching during a chat, and the Brazilian Portuguese translations. Sentiment leads: r/OpenWebUI threads exist for the 0.13.x cycle but the fetch of the 0.13.1 thread returned 403, so no community tier source is cited anywhere. The Instagram post announcing the feature was seen only as a search snippet and is not treated as fetched.
viewer_situation: You have Open WebUI running with your models at home and you have watched a coding agent work in a chat, but every one of those runs started because you sat there and typed.
process_steps: Connect an Open Terminal under Settings > Admin > Integrations (or sign into Tether so your own computer appears under Your devices in the terminal menu).
Create the automation under User Menu > Automations with the New Automation button.
Choose the terminal, pick the working folder, and select the coding agent available there.
Set the schedule (Once, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or a custom RRULE) and write instructions that say exactly what to do and what not to.
Click Run now once and read the chat it creates before trusting the schedule.
Check the run-history entry for success or error, and leave the automation enabled only once the output is something you can judge in seconds.
objection: You are handing an unattended agent full tool approval on a real folder -- nobody is there to click Allow -- and a scheduled prompt is a thin spec for code changes.
